payload.question: When someone is threatened with homelessness, does the council find them somewhere?
payload.label: Homelessness prevention duties ending in suitable housing, Q1 2025/26
payload.council_caveat: The council raised its own target for this indicator during this quarter and warns that the traffic lights on earlier quarters were set against the old thresholds: "Please note: The target and interventions levels for this KPI were updated in Q1 2025/26. RAG rating prior to this reflect previous thresholds." It does not publish what the old target was. Its reason for raising it: "Over the past three years, average performance has been 78%, demonstrating consistent excellence. In light of this, we have raised the target to 75% which sets a higher standard and enables earlier identification of any dips in performance." The council publishes these numbers as screenshots of a dashboard inside a PDF, so they cannot be read by machine. We read them off the images by eye, which is why this measure is flagged for human checking.
payload.evidence: If you are about to lose your home, the council has a legal duty to try to prevent it. This counts the cases where that duty ended because somewhere suitable was found. The council aims for 75% and reached 82% in the first quarter of 2025/26.
